raw_record.support_text: Diethylnitrosamine (DEN) is described as a chemical carcinogen, and DEN-induced HCC in the rat is presented as a well accepted model for hepatocarcinogenesis. raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Induction protocol included partial hepatectomy-initiated hepatic cell proliferation, a necrotizing dose of carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄), and phenobarbitone sodium during the induction period.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN is hydroxylated to alpha-hydroxy nitrosamine by cytochrome P450, which alkylates DNA; ROS generated during this process drive lipid peroxidation contributing to hepatocarcinogenesis. Cited reference [1].

raw_record.support_text: In a long-term follow-up of rheumatoid arthritis patients treated with oral cyclophosphamide (CYC), 9 cases of bladder cancer were observed versus 0.4 expected (relative risk 22, 95% CI 8.8-55.5). The authors conclude that bladder cancer was significantly more frequent in the CYC-treated group than in the control group, and that the increased risk of malignancy persists into the second decade after discontinuing CYC.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: rheumatoid arthritis patients treated with oral CYC
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Population was rheumatoid arthritis patients; risk increased with total dose and duration of CYC treatment.
raw_record.extra_details: Relative risk 22 (95% CI 8.8-55.5); latency mean 156 months (range 4.0-22.8 years); incidence compared with western Pennsylvania age- and sex-specific rates; original 10-year followup study reference (14).

raw_record.support_text: In the 2-year rat carcinogenicity study with canagliflozin, a higher incidence of pheochromocytomas (adrenal medullary tumors) was observed in males compared to females. The pheochromocytomas were attributed to a mechanism involving carbohydrate malabsorption-mediated calcium dysregulation (SGLT1 inhibition). Adrenal medullary tumors were not observed in the 2-year mouse carcinogenicity study with canagliflozin. Based on species differences, exposure safety multiples (5-7x clinical dose), and experience with sugar/sugar alcohols, the rat pheochromocytomas were not expected to have safety implications in humans.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Rat-specific; higher incidence in males; attributed to carbohydrate malabsorption/SGLT1-inhibition-induced calcium dysregulation; not observed in the 2-year mouse study; deemed not expected to have human safety implications (species differences, 5-7x human exposure multiples); high dose 100 mg/kg (~12x male, ~21x female multiples).
raw_record.extra_details: Mechanism hypothesized to be carbohydrate malabsorption mediated calcium dysregulation; similar to poorly digestible sugars and sugar alcohols (lactose, sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol, lactitol); references [7,8,32].

raw_record.support_text: Bladder cancer cases related to benzidine production or use were reported from the Peoples Republic of China: 30 bladder cancer cases among approximately 2,000 Chinese workers (30-fold elevated bladder cancer risk due to occupation), and a 35-fold increased risk in a cohort of 784 benzidine-exposed workers, increasing up to 75-fold in work areas with exceptionally high exposures. Benzidine's high carcinogenic potential to the urinary bladder underlies elevated bladder cancer risks in workers exposed to benzidine-based dyes with lower exposures.
